lesson_plan.title: What does a spectral similarity score establish?

learning_objectives.description: Explain how precursor mass changes the matching of two spectra.
Distinguish a numerical similarity result from a stronger chemical identification claim and state the missing evidence.

concepts.title: Precursor-aware spectral evidence
concepts.description: The matching rule affects a score; interpretation requires knowing how the score was obtained.

corpus_refs.title: SimMS: a GPU-accelerated cosine similarity implementation for tandem mass spectrometry.

scene_outlines.title: What information enters the similarity calculation?
scene_outlines.notes: Read the selected introduction excerpt. This is the sole captured passage; no whole-paper coverage is claimed.

scene_outlines.title: Explore direct and precursor-aware matching
scene_outlines.notes: Harness creates an external viewer for the existing illustrative spectra. Ask for a prediction, vary one parameter, inspect matched peaks. An actual fixture computation is not a replication of SimMS or an identification benchmark. No capsule is selected by this draft.

scene_outlines.title: What can you conclude from the score?
scene_outlines.notes: Proposed teaching extension for human review: critique a claim that a changed matching score by itself certifies chemical identity. Request independent evidence and the learner's own confidence. Do not label this inference as a direct finding of the captured excerpt. A teacher must supply and validate any assessment key and transfer task.

source_links.quote: “Modified” cosine similarity is an extension of greedy cosine that uses the precursor mass as an additional input

viewers.goal: Expose the role of the matching rule and preserve the distinction between measured baseline and derived exploration.
interactions: Record the learner's interpretation and confidence without automatic grading
